title: Donor Lifecycle, Testing Status & Replacement Decisions

content.overview: Specialist instruction for donor lifecycle, testing status & replacement decisions in donor/mother plant systems.

sections.title: Track donor status over time
sections.body: Maintain identity, age or establishment date, testing status, major plant-health events, propagation output, performance trend, holds and disposition decisions as a longitudinal record.

sections.title: Testing status must be specific
sections.body: A negative result is meaningful only with the target, method, sample identity and date. 'Clean' should not be used as an undefined permanent status.

sections.title: Replacement decisions need documented rationale
sections.body: Declining performance, repeated health concerns, identity uncertainty or validated lifecycle policy may support replacement, but the record should preserve why the decision was made and what happened to downstream material.

commonMistakes: Treating visual health as proof of clean-stock status.
content.practicalApplication: Review a donor-management scenario, preserve identity and status evidence, and document the strongest supported next action without overstating cause or cleanliness.
content.summary: Donor management depends on traceable identity, plant-health evidence, controlled movement and longitudinal performance records.
